title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing

items.title: Finite probability vectors
proof_obligations: Specify the finite nonempty alphabet, nonnegative coordinates, normalization, and zero coordinates.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite nonempty set. A **probability vector** on
$\mathcal X$ is a family $P=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$ of real numbers such that
$p_x\ge 0$ for every $x$ and $\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x=1$. Its support is
$\operatorname{supp}P:=\{x\in\mathcal X:p_x>0\}$. Coordinates outside the
support are retained as zeros; they are not deleted from the alphabet.

For another probability vector $Q=(q_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, the notation
$P\ll Q$ means $\operatorname{supp}P\subseteq\operatorname{supp}Q$. All
finite sums over $\mathcal X$ use the displayed alphabet and ordinary finite
real arithmetic, extended to $+\infty$ only where a later definition says so.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 1, §1.2
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §I-A

items.title: Boundary limits of a normalized finite convex generator
proof_obligations: Prove existence of the zero boundary value and recession limit as extended-real limits, excluding negative infinity.
items.statement:
Let $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be convex and satisfy $f(1)=0$. Then both
extended-real limits
$$f(0):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t),\qquad
f_\infty:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(t)}t$$
exist in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$; neither limit is $-\infty$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.1
Igal Sason and Sergio Verdú, f-Divergence Inequalities, §II-B, equations (35)–(39)

items.title: The finite KL generator has the required convex boundary extension
items.statement:
For $f(t)=t\log t$ on $t>0$, one has $f(1)=0$, $f$ is convex on
$(0,\infty)$, $\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t)=0$, and
$\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t=+\infty$.
proof_obligations: Use logarithm differentiability and the second-derivative convexity criterion on (0,∞).
Verify the 0+ boundary limit with log t/t→0 and the recession limit from log monotonicity and surjectivity.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.1
Igal Sason and Sergio Verdú, f-Divergence Inequalities, §II-B, equations (43)–(45)

items.title: The finite Rényi generators are convex with stated boundary values
items.statement:
For $\alpha>1$, the generator $h_\alpha(t)=t^\alpha-1$ is convex on
$(0,\infty)$, satisfies $h_\alpha(1)=0$, has
$h_\alpha(0+)=-1$, and has recession limit
$\lim_{t\to\infty}h_\alpha(t)/t=+\infty$. For $0<\alpha<1$, the generator
$g_\alpha(t)=1-t^\alpha$ is convex on $(0,\infty)$, satisfies
$g_\alpha(1)=0$, has $g_\alpha(0+)=1$, and has recession limit
$\lim_{t\to\infty}g_\alpha(t)/t=0$.
proof_obligations: Derive convexity from the second derivatives for each order range.
Prove endpoint and recession limits with the positive-power representation and log/exponential limits.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1 and 7.12
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-A

items.title: Finite f-divergence with support conventions
proof_obligations: State the convex generator class and both boundary limits.
Define zero and singular-support contributions without an ambiguous 0 times infinity.
items.statement:
Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]). A **convex
generator** is a finite convex function $f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ with
$f(1)=0$; convexity uses the two-point inequality of
[[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]. Use its
extended boundary values
$$f(0):=\lim_{t\downarrow0}f(t),\qquad f_\infty:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{f(t)}t.$$
These limits exist in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ by
[[lem-convex-generator-boundary-limits-exist]]. Define the **finite
f-divergence from $P$ to $Q$**
by
$$D_f(P\|Q):=\sum_{x:q_x>0}q_x f(p_x/q_x)+
f_\infty\sum_{x:q_x=0}p_x.$$
In the first sum, if $p_x=0$, the term means $q_x f(0)$. A coordinate with
$p_x=q_x=0$ contributes zero and is omitted. The second term is defined as
zero when its coefficient $\sum_{q_x=0}p_x$ is zero, even if
$f_\infty=+\infty$; if that coefficient is positive and $f_\infty=+\infty$,
the divergence is $+\infty$.

The boundary term is essential when $P\not\ll Q$. It is the recession
contribution of the generator and is not the value $f(0)$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.1, Definition 7.1
Igal Sason and Sergio Verdú, f-Divergence Inequalities, §II-B, Definition 3 and equations (35)–(39)

items.title: Finite type-II testing function with explicit orientation
proof_obligations: Fix P as the null and Q as the alternative.
Define the rejection function, type-I constraint, and type-II objective; show the infimum is a real number.
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$
([[def-finite-probability-vector]]). Test the simple null $H_0:P$ against the
simple alternative $H_1:Q$. A randomized test is a function
$\phi:\mathcal X\to[0,1]$, where $\phi(x)$ is the probability of rejecting
$H_0$ after observing $x$; thus $1-\phi(x)$ is the probability of accepting
$H_0$ ([[def-randomized-test]]). Its type-I error is
$\sum_xp_x\phi(x)$, and its type-II error is
$\sum_xq_x(1-\phi(x))$ ([[def-test-size-and-power]]).

For $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, define the oriented type-II testing function
$$\beta_\epsilon(P,Q):=\inf_{\substack{\phi:\mathcal X\to[0,1]\\\sum_xp_x\phi(x)\le\epsilon}}\sum_xq_x(1-\phi(x)).$$
Here the first argument is the null law and the second is the alternative
law; $\epsilon$ bounds rejection under the first law, while the objective is
acceptance of the null under the second. The feasible set is nonempty
because $\phi=0$ is allowed, and every objective value lies in $[0,1]$, so
the infimum is a real number in that interval. In the
Neyman–Pearson-region convention that constrains null acceptance below by
$\gamma$, this is the lower boundary value at $\gamma=1-\epsilon$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 14, §14.1, Definition 14.1
Finite-sample tests, Neyman–Pearson and Valid P-values, definitions of randomized test and test size/power

items.title: Finite stochastic kernels
proof_obligations: Fix the input/output alphabets and the row-stochastic convention.
Define the induced output law with the input-first kernel convention.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be finite nonempty sets. A **stochastic kernel**
from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ is a matrix
$K=(K(y\mid x))_{x\in\mathcal X,y\in\mathcal Y}$ such that
$K(y\mid x)\ge0$ and $\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}K(y\mid x)=1$ for every
$x\in\mathcal X$. The convention is input first in the condition and output
first in the value $K(y\mid x)$.

For a probability vector $P=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}$, the output vector
$PK$ on $\mathcal Y$ is
$$(PK)_y:=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xK(y\mid x).$$
It is a probability vector because its coordinates are nonnegative and
$\sum_y(PK)_y=\sum_xp_x\sum_yK(y\mid x)=\sum_xp_x=1$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1–7.2
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-B

items.title: Finite Kullback–Leibler divergence
proof_obligations: State the natural-log convention and the p-positive/q-zero infinity branch.
Identify KL with the f-divergence generated by t log t.
items.statement:
For probability vectors $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ on the same finite
nonempty alphabet, their **Kullback–Leibler divergence** (or **relative
entropy**) in the stated direction from $P$ to $Q$ is
$$D(P\|Q):=\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x\log\frac{p_x}{q_x}.$$
The logarithm is natural. If $p_x>0$ and $q_x=0$ for at least one $x$, set
$D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $p_x=0$, its contribution is zero, including when
$q_x=0$; equivalently, $0\log(0/q_x)=0$. When $P\ll Q$, all ratios in the
sum are positive and finite.

The generator $f(t)=t\log t$ is admissible for
[[def-finite-f-divergence]] by
[[lem-finite-kl-generator-is-admissible]]. Its boundary values
$f(0)=0$ and $f_\infty=+\infty$ make that f-divergence exactly the displayed
KL formula, including the singular-support case.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.1
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §I-A and Theorem 5

items.title: The closed convex perspective is subadditive
proof_obligations: Define the perspective at (0,0), on the positive b-axis, and on the singular boundary b=0.
Prove the finite-sum inequality for both positive total second coordinate and total second coordinate zero.
items.statement:
Let $f$ be a convex generator from [[def-finite-f-divergence]]. Define its
closed perspective on $a,b\ge0$ by
$$
\Pi_f(a,b):=\begin{cases}
b f(a/b),&b>0,\ a>0,\\
b f(0),&b>0,\ a=0,\\
a f_\infty,&b=0,\ a>0,\\
0,&a=b=0.
\end{cases}
$$
For every finite family $(a_i,b_i)\in[0,\infty)^2$,
$$\Pi_f\!\left(\sum_i a_i,\sum_i b_i\right)\le\sum_i\Pi_f(a_i,b_i).$$

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.1
Igal Sason and Sergio Verdú, f-Divergence Inequalities, §II-B, equations (35)–(39)

items.title: Finite Rényi divergence
proof_obligations: State the order range, the order-one value, and support/zero conventions for orders below and above one.
Define the zero-affinity case as extended value +infinity.
items.statement:
Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on the same finite
nonempty alphabet. For order $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$ with $\alpha\ne1$, put
$$S_\alpha(P,Q):=\sum_{x:q_x>0}p_x^\alpha q_x^{1-\alpha}.$$
If $\alpha>1$ and $p_x>0=q_x$ for some $x$, define
$S_\alpha(P,Q)=+\infty$; if $0<\alpha<1$, such coordinates contribute
zero. In the displayed sum, $p_x=0<q_x$ contributes zero. If the sum is
zero, then necessarily $\alpha<1$ and the logarithmic expression below is
defined as $+\infty$. The **Rényi divergence of order $\alpha$ from $P$ to
$Q$** is
$$D_\alpha(P\|Q):=\frac{\log S_\alpha(P,Q)}{\alpha-1}.$$
At order one define
$$D_1(P\|Q):=D(P\|Q),$$
using [[def-finite-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. All divergences are
extended-real-valued; the direction is always first argument to second.

For $0<\alpha<1$, a point with $p_x>0=q_x$ contributes zero to the affinity
$S_\alpha$ rather than infinity. For $\alpha>1$, the same support mismatch
makes $D_\alpha(P\|Q)=+\infty$. The sign of $\alpha-1$ is part of the
definition and reverses inequalities when $0<\alpha<1$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.12, Definition 7.22
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-A, Definition 2

items.title: Finite iid log-likelihood averages concentrate
proof_obligations: Assume P is absolutely continuous with respect to Q on the finite alphabet.
Use boundedness on supp(P), independence, variance additivity, and Chebyshev's inequality.
items.statement:
Let $P=(p_x)$ and $Q=(q_x)$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty
alphabet with $P\ll Q$. For $n\ge1$, write
$P^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_i p_{x_i}$ and
$Q^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_i q_{x_i}$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent
with common law $P$, define $\ell(x)=\log(p_x/q_x)$ when $p_x>0$ and
$\ell(x)=0$ when $p_x=0$, and put $L_n=\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(X_i)$. Then
$L_n/n\to D(P\|Q)$ in probability as $n\to\infty$. For every
$x^n\in\operatorname{supp}(P)^n$, one also has
$Q^n(x^n)=P^n(x^n)\exp(-L_n(x^n))$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 14, §14.1, proof of Theorem 14.13
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-C, Theorem 5

items.title: Finite data processing for f-divergences
proof_obligations: Apply perspective subadditivity at each output symbol.
Use positive homogeneity and the row-sum-one kernel identity.
Retain singular support terms.
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$,
let $K$ be a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X$ to a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal Y$, and let $f$ be a convex generator as in
[[def-finite-f-divergence]]. Then
$$D_f(PK\|QK)\le D_f(P\|Q),$$
with both divergences interpreted using the zero and singular-support
conventions of that definition.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.2, Theorem 7.3
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §§II-B–III-A

items.title: Finite data processing for Kullback–Leibler divergence
proof_obligations: Use the t log t generator and check its recession term at infinity.
Show the f-divergence specialization is exactly the stated KL convention.
items.statement:
For probability vectors $P,Q$ on a finite nonempty alphabet and a stochastic
kernel $K$ to another finite nonempty alphabet,
$$D(PK\|QK)\le D(P\|Q).$$

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1–7.2
Igal Sason and Sergio Verdú, f-Divergence Inequalities, §II-B, equations (43)–(45)

items.title: Finite data processing for Rényi divergence
proof_obligations: Treat 0<alpha<1 and alpha>1 separately because division by alpha−1 reverses order below one.
Use the convex generators 1−t^alpha and t^alpha−1 respectively.
Handle infinite divergences and zero affinity explicitly.
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$
and let $K$ be a stochastic kernel from $\mathcal X$ to a finite nonempty
alphabet $\mathcal Y$. For every $\alpha\in(0,\infty)\setminus\{1\}$,
$$D_\alpha(PK\|QK)\le D_\alpha(P\|Q),$$
with Rényi divergence as defined in [[def-finite-renyi-divergence]].

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1–7.2 and §7.12
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §§II-A, II-B, III-A

items.title: The finite Rényi divergence limit is KL
proof_obligations: Handle P not absolutely continuous with respect to Q on both sides of order one.
For P absolutely continuous with respect to Q, differentiate the finite positive-support sum at one.
items.statement:
For probability vectors $P,Q$ on a finite nonempty alphabet,
$$\lim_{\alpha\to1}D_\alpha(P\|Q)=D(P\|Q)$$
as a two-sided extended-real limit.

references.title: Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-C, Theorem 5 and proof
Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §7.12

items.title: KL is the iid type-II testing exponent
proof_obligations: For P not absolutely continuous with respect to Q, construct an eventually feasible zero-type-II test.
For P absolutely continuous with respect to Q, prove both exponent bounds using the explicit likelihood ratio.
Use the named testing orientation P=null, Q=alternative and epsilon as the type-I upper bound.
items.statement:
Let $P,Q$ be probability vectors on a finite nonempty alphabet $\mathcal X$.
For $n\ge1$, write $P^n,Q^n$ for the product vectors on $\mathcal X^n$,
with $P^n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_{i=1}^np_{x_i}$ and similarly for $Q^n$.
For every fixed $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, with $\beta_\epsilon$ oriented as in
[[def-finite-hypothesis-testing-beta]],
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}-\frac1n\log\beta_\epsilon(P^n,Q^n)=D(P\|Q),$$
where $-\log0:=+\infty$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 14, §14.1, Theorem 14.13 and proof

title: F-Divergences, Rényi Information, and Hypothesis Testing — Examples

items.title: A binary Neyman–Pearson boundary randomization
proof_obligations: Specify null and alternative orientation and the type-I/type-II conventions.
Verify exact boundary randomization and prove the finite optimization directly.
Show the likelihood-ratio threshold uses Q/P, consistent with rejecting the null P in favor of Q.
items.statement:
Let the null law be $P=(2/3,1/3)$ and the alternative law be $Q=(1/3,2/3)$
on $\mathcal X=\{a,b\}$. For the type-I bound $\epsilon=1/2$, the optimal
test rejects with probability $1/4$ at $a$ and probability $1$ at $b$.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 14, §§14.1 and 14.3

items.title: Binary f-, KL-, and Rényi divergences
proof_obligations: Compute KL, order-1/2 and order-2 Rényi values for the stated binary laws.
Check the total-variation generator with the repository's one-half normalization.
items.statement:
On $\mathcal X=\{0,1\}$, take $P=(3/4,1/4)$ and $Q=(1/4,3/4)$. Their
supports agree and all coordinates are positive.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1 and 7.12
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §§I-A and II-A

items.title: Disjoint supports and singular divergence values
proof_obligations: Evaluate zero-support terms for total variation, KL, and all positive Rényi orders.
Explain why no 0 times infinity contribution is introduced.
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal X=\{a,b\}$, $P=(1,0)$, and $Q=(0,1)$. The two laws have
disjoint supports.

references.title: Yury Polyanskiy and Yihong Wu, Information Theory: From Coding to Learning, Chapter 7, §§7.1 and 7.12
Tim van Erven and Peter Harremoës, Rényi Divergence and Kullback-Leibler Divergence, §II-A
